record.title: The planar graph absolute clique number conjecture for (m,n)-colored mixed graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the family of planar graphs, and let $\omega_{a(m,n)}(\mathcal{P})$ denote its $(m,n)$-absolute clique number.

**Planar absolute clique number conjecture.** For the family $\mathcal{P}$ of planar graphs,

$$
\omega_{a(m,n)}(\mathcal{P}) = 3(2m+n)^2+(2m+n)+1
$$

for all $(m,n) \neq (0,1)$.

The preceding argument gives the general upper bound $|G| \leq 9(2m+n)^2+2(2m+n)+2$ for an $(m,n)$-colored mixed planar graph, while the conjecture proposes the exact value of the absolute clique number. Its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Nondegeneracy of random regular Tanner graphs with logarithmic girth
record.statement: Let $d_c>d_v\geq 3$ be integers satisfying $d_v<\beta_{d_c}d_c$, where $\beta_{d_c}$ is Calkin's threshold. For a positive constant $\lambda$, let $\Gamma_{\lambda}$ be the ensemble of $(d_v,d_c)$-regular Tanner graphs on $n$ variable nodes with girth at least $\lambda\log n$. **Nondegeneracy conjecture.** There is a sufficiently small constant $\lambda>0$ such that, for every constant $c>0$, a random graph $G$ from $\Gamma_{\lambda}$ is $(c\log n,\omega(1))$-nondegenerate with high probability. This conjecture concerns the rigidity condition: for graphs of logarithmic girth and minimum check degree at least three, the stated nondegeneracy property is equivalent to the simpler rigidity condition discussed in the paper.

record.title: The conjectural formula for the geography constant of surfaces of general type in characteristic p
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $\kappa_p$ be the infimum of $\chi/c_1^2$ over minimal algebraic surfaces of general type defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. **Conjectural formula for $\kappa_p$.** If $p\geq 5$, then

$$
\kappa_p=\frac{p^2-4p-1}{4(3p^2-8p-3)}.
$$

This conjectural formula gives the optimal lower bound for $\chi$ in terms of $c_1^2$ in characteristic $p$. The paper proves positivity for $p>2$, a lower bound for $p\geq 7$, the limit $\lim_{p\to\infty}\kappa_p=1/12$, and the exact value $\kappa_5=1/32$, but does not establish the displayed formula in general.

record.title: Maximum-efficiency conjecture for practical multi-user OFDM systems
record.statement:
Let a practical multi-user OFDM system have $K$ users and $N$ subcarriers, with the number of subcarriers less than $2{,}002$, and let $d_{max}$ denote its maximum efficiency.

**Maximum-efficiency conjecture.** The maximum efficiency is $d_{max}=1.4998$, achieved when there are $K=3$ users using $N=2{,}001$ subcarriers.

This statement identifies the best efficiency found by the paper's analysis for practical systems subject to the stated subcarrier limit. The source does not provide evidence that the claim has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Garijo–González–Márquez conjecture on location-domination in twin-free connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $\lambda_{|\mathcal C^*}(n)$ denote the maximum location-domination number of a twin-free, connected graph on $n$ vertices. **Garijo–González–Márquez conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $n_1$ such that, for every $n\ge n_1$, 

$$
\lambda_{|\mathcal C^*}(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

Garijo, González, and Márquez proved the matching lower bound for every $n\ge14$; the conjecture asserts that this lower bound is eventually exact.

record.title: Degree-sequence conjecture for spanning triangulations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with degree sequence $d_1\leq\dots\leq d_n$. A **spanning triangulation** is a maximal planar graph spanning all vertices of $G$.

**Degree-sequence conjecture for spanning triangulations.** For every $\eta>0$, there exists $n_0\in\mathbb N$ such that, whenever $n\geq n_0$ and

$$
d_i\geq \frac n3+i+\eta n\qquad\text{for all }i\leq \frac n3,
$$

$G$ contains a spanning triangulation.

This would extend known minimum-degree results on spanning triangulations and is presented in the paper as an open consequence suggested by its degree-sequence theorem.

record.title: Equality conjecture for the h-critical bound in Theorem cor h=3
record.statement: Let $n$ and $m$ be the parameters occurring in Theorem cor h=3, whose bound concerns the quantity $\rho(\mathbb{Z}_n,m,3)$ and its upper estimate in terms of $u(n,m,3)$. **Equality conjecture.** For all $n$ and $m$, equality holds in Theorem cor h=3. This conjecture was previously made in the cited work and would determine the relevant bound for the $h$-critical number when $h=3$; its resolution is not indicated here.

record.title: The worst-case value conjecture for Tron on cycles
record.statement: Let an instance of \texttt{Tron} on a cycle be a game instance whose underlying graph is a cycle, with arbitrary vertex weights. The **cycle value conjecture.** Any instance of \texttt{Tron} on a cycle has value at most $1/5$. The paper notes that the worst weighted-tree value is $1/5$ and that the worst weighted cycle known to the authors also has value $1/5$; determining the maximum value for cycles remains open.

record.title: The exact balancing-set conjecture for vectors with pth roots of unity
record.statement:
Let $n$ be an arbitrary integer and let $p$ be a prime factor of $n$. Let $\omega_1=e^{\frac{2\pi i}{p}}$, define $\omega_i=\omega_1^i$ for $0\leq i\leq p-1$, and set

$$
B=\{1,\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_{p-1}\}^n\subseteq\mathbb C^n.
$$

Let $K(n,p)$ be the minimum $k$ for which there exist vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in B$ such that for every $w\in B$, some $v_i$ satisfies $v_i\cdot w=0$.

**Exact balancing-set conjecture.** For every integer $n$ and every prime factor $p$ of $n$,

$$
K(n,p)=n(p-1).
$$

The paper proves the lower bound $K(n,p)\geq n(p-1)$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is attained, giving the exact minimum size of a family of vectors that balances every vector in $B$.
record.source_name: Gábor Hegedüs, “Balancing Sets of Vectors”, arXiv:1412.5394 (2014).

record.title: The asymptotically optimal algebraic-connectivity bound for bounded-degree trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $d$. The **asymptotically optimal tree bound conjecture.** As $n\rightarrow\infty$ for fixed $d$,

$$
\lambda_{2}(T)\leq\frac{d(d-2)}{d-1}\frac{1}{n}+O\left(\frac{\ln n}{n^{2}}\right).
$$

Here $\lambda_{2}(T)$ denotes the algebraic connectivity of $T$. The conjecture improves the paper's preceding general bound and is known in the source for the well-balanced Bethe trees; its validity for all trees with maximum degree $d$ remains open.

record.title: The extremal average communicability angle conjecture for connected graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ nodes. Write $P_n$ for the path graph on $n$ nodes, $K_n$ for the complete graph on $n$ nodes, and let the average communicability angle be the average of the communicability angles over pairs of nodes. **Extremal communicability-angle conjecture.** Among all connected graphs with $n$ nodes, the average communicability angle is largest for $P_n$ and smallest for $K_n$. The claim is motivated by verification for all connected graphs with 5, 6, 7, and 8 nodes; its general validity remains open.

record.title: The interval conjecture for region counts of circles with pairwise intersections
record.statement: Let $C_n$ be the set of numbers of regions formed by $n$ circles in the plane, in an arrangement not in general position, such that every two circles have at least one common point. Let $L_n$ be the set of numbers of regions formed by $n$ distinct lines in the plane in an arrangement not in general position. The maximal elements of $L_n$ and $C_n$ are respectively $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1$ and $n(n-1)+2$. **Interval conjecture.** The set $C_n$ contains every integer in the interval from $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}+1$ through $n(n-1)+2$. This would determine a complete consecutive range of attainable region counts for the circle arrangements under consideration, extending the relation between the possible counts for circles and lines; the supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: The max-cut local concentration conjecture for random graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph. An ordinary max cut is a partition of the vertex set into two parts attaining the maximum possible number of crossing edges. **Max-cut local concentration conjecture.** If

$$
p\gg n^{-1}\log n,
$$

then with high probability no ordinary max cut of $G_{n,p}$ contains all, or even $51\%$, of the edges incident with any vertex. The source notes that a weaker bound is known for $r\geq 4$, while the asserted range is not established there; for $r=3$ even the bound $p>Cn^{-1/2}$ was not known.

record.title: The mixed eigenvalue ordering conjecture for triangles
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a triangle with side lengths $L$, $M$ and $S$ satisfying $L\geq M\geq S$. For a chosen set of sides, let $\lambda_1^{\mathrm{set}}$ be the smallest eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on those sides and Neumann conditions on the remaining sides; in particular, $\lambda_1^S$, $\lambda_1^M$, $\lambda_1^L$ and $\lambda_1^{MS}$ have the corresponding meanings.

**Mixed eigenvalue ordering conjecture.** For an arbitrary triangle,

$$
\lambda_1^S<\lambda_1^M<\lambda_1^L<\lambda_1^{MS},
$$

as long as the appropriate sides have different lengths.

This conjecture would complete the ordering of the mixed Dirichlet–Neumann eigenvalues left unresolved by the theorem above. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Monotonicity of the minimum degree of minimal Ramsey graphs in the clique size
record.statement:
Let $s_r(K_k)$ denote the minimum degree of an $r$-edge-coloured graph that is minimal Ramsey for $K_k$, with $r\geqslant 3$ and $k\geqslant 3$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** For all $r\geqslant 3$ and $k\geqslant 3$,

$$
s_r(K_k)\geqslant s_r(K_{k-1}).
$$

The claim expresses the expectation that graphs Ramsey for larger cliques should require at least as large a minimum degree. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: The 1-uniqueness conjecture for critical graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a critical graph, meaning that it has tree-depth $k$ for some $k$ and every proper minor of $G$ has smaller tree-depth. A graph is **1-unique** if, for every vertex $v$ of $G$, some optimal ranking of $G$ has $v$ as the unique vertex with label $1$. **The 1-uniqueness conjecture.** Every critical graph is 1-unique. The source says that this conjecture implies the maximum-degree conjecture and gives no resolution of it; the paper studies classes satisfying it.

record.title: Chow's stability conjecture for holomorphic newforms
record.statement: Let $q$ be a positive squarefree integer, let $k$ be a positive even integer, and let $n_0(q,k)$ be the least integer such that equality of Hecke eigenvalues at all primes $p\leq n_0(q,k)$ forces two holomorphic newforms of weight $k$, level $q$, and principal character to be equal. **Chow's stability conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $k_0$ such that for all $k\geq k_0$, $n_0(q,k)$ is the smallest prime not dividing $q$. The conjecture is based on numerical calculations for many small squarefree levels; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Periodic-limit conjecture for normalized curve-diagram counts
record.statement:
Let $g_{n,k}$ denote the number of curve diagrams of genus $n$ and complexity $k$, as in the paper. Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. **Periodic-limit conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $\rho_n$ such that, for every integer $\ell\in\{0,1,\ldots,\rho_n-1\}$, the sequence

$$
\frac{g_{n,k\rho_n+\ell}}{k^{2(n-2)}}
$$

has a positive limit $\lambda_{n,\ell}$ as $k\to+\infty$. This stronger conjecture is motivated by numerical patterns suggesting that the normalized counts split into convergent clusters according to a residue class of $k$; the paper mentions moduli $6$ for $n=4$ and $2$ for $n=5$, while the corresponding cases $n=2$ and $n=3$ exhibit related patterns.

record.title: Asciak's edge-reconstruction number conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, connected, $r$-regular graph with $r\geq 3$. Its **edge-reconstruction number** $ern(G)$ is the smallest size of a subset of its edge-deck from which $G$ is reconstructable.

**Asciak's conjecture.**

$$
ern(G)\leq 2.
$$

This conjecture concerns how many edge-cards suffice to reconstruct a regular graph. It was originally published in K. J. Asciak's 1999 master's thesis and republished in a 2010 survey of open questions in reconstruction numbers; it remains open.

record.title: Conjecture on the distance parameter for three longest paths with two transition vertices
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, let $\mathcal{L}(G)$ be the set of longest paths of $G$, and let $f(G,\mathcal{P})$ be the minimum, over vertices $v\in V(G)$, of $\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}d_G(v,V(P))$. For each $P\in\mathcal{P}$, let $t_{\mathcal{P}}(P)$ denote the parameter defined in the paper. **The conjecture.** If $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{L}(G)$, $|\mathcal{P}|=3$, and some $P\in\mathcal{P}$ satisfies $t_{\mathcal{P}}(P)=2$, then

$$
f(G,\mathcal{P})=0.
$$

The paper notes that this would improve the upper bound for $f(G,\mathcal{P})$ in its preceding theorem to $(2n+12)/27$. The conjecture is presented as open, and its notation depends on definitions given elsewhere in the paper.
record.source_name: Shinya Fujita, Michitaka Furuya, Reza Naserasr and Kenta Ozeki, “A New Approach Towards a Conjecture on Intersecting Three Longest Paths”, arXiv:1503.01219 (2015).

record.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the carousel homomorphism maximizer
record.statement:
Let $R_{2n+1}$ be the odd carousel tournament, let $\phi_R$ be the carousel homomorphism, and let $\operatorname{Hom}^+({\mathcal{A}}^0,\mathbb{R})$ denote the positive homomorphisms of the tournament algebra.

**Carousel maximizer uniqueness conjecture.** For every $n\geq2$, a homomorphism $\phi\in\operatorname{Hom}^+({\mathcal{A}}^0,\mathbb{R})$ maximizes the density of $R_{2n+1}$ if and only if $\phi=\phi_R$.
This is presented as a consequence of the preceding maximum-density conjecture and asserts uniqueness of the maximizer for all $n\geq2$; it remains open.

record.title: Gao–Thangadurai–Kubertin conjecture for finite abelian $p$-groups
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $G$ be a finite abelian $p$-group, and write $q=\exp(G)$. For a positive integer $k$, let $s_{kq}(G)$ be the smallest length such that every sequence over $G$ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $kq$, and let $D(G)$ denote the Davenport constant of $G$. **Gao–Thangadurai–Kubertin conjecture.** For every $k\geq1$,

$$
s_{kq}(G)=kq+D(G)-1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the exact threshold for prescribed-length zero-sum subsequences in finite abelian $p$-groups. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved; its status is therefore recorded as open.

record.title: Wu's divisibility-by-3 conjecture for symmetric concatenations
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ be the smallest prime obtained by inserting $n$ between two copies of a positive-length string of identical decimal digits, or $0$ if no such prime exists. A positive integer is a **multiple of $11$** when it is divisible by $11$.

**Wu's divisibility-by-3 conjecture.** If $n$ is not a multiple of $11$ with an even number of digits and $a(n)=0$, then $n$ is a multiple of $3$.

This is proposed after the original OEIS conjecture has been shown false. The paper reports computational examples supporting the claim, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

record.title: The OEIS A256480 conjecture for prepended-digit primes
record.statement:
Let $b(n)$ be the smallest prime obtained by appending $n$ to a positive-length string of identical decimal digits, or $0$ if no such prime exists.

**OEIS A256480 conjecture.**

$$
b(n)=0
$$

if and only if $n$ is even or $n$ is divisible by $5$.

The necessary condition is immediate from the final digit of a prime candidate, while the converse is proposed for all remaining $n$. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: The list colouring conjecture for chromatic index
record.statement:
An instance of list edge-colouring consists of a graph $G$ and an assignment of lists $L:E(G)\rightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{N})$, where each edge $e$ receives a list $L(e)$ of colours. An $L$-edge-colouring assigns to each edge $e$ a colour in $L(e)$ so that adjacent edges receive different colours. The **list chromatic index** $\mathrm{ch}'(G)$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that every assignment of lists of size at least $k$ admits an $L$-edge-colouring; $\chi'(G)$ denotes the chromatic index of $G$. **List colouring conjecture.** For all graphs $G$ it holds that

$$
\mathrm{ch}'(G)=\chi'(G).
$$

This is a central open problem in list colouring. It has been verified asymptotically by Kahn and for particular families, including bipartite graphs by Galvin, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Richard Lang, “On the list chromatic index of graphs of tree-width 3 and maximum degree at least 7”, arXiv:1504.02122 (2015).

record.title: The eigenvalue bound for interpolating graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_{n,a}$ be the graphs considered in the paper, with largest eigenvalue denoted by $\lambda_{n,a}$. The parameters satisfy $n\geq 1$ and $a\geq 2$.

**Eigenvalue bound conjecture.** For all graphs $G_{n,a}$, we have

$$
\lambda_{n,a} \leq (a-1)\log_a n,
$$

with equality if and only if $n$ is a power of $a$.

This conjecture extends the theorem proved in the paper from $a=2$ to general $a$. Its status is not determined by the supplied text.

record.title: Extremality of disjoint unions of complete bipartite graphs for k-dominating independent sets
record.statement:
Let $k>3$ and let $n$ be divisible by $2k$. Consider $n$-vertex graphs and the number of their $k$-dominating independent sets.

**Complete-bipartite-union conjecture.** The maximum number of $k$-dominating independent sets in an $n$-vertex graph is attained by the disjoint union of $n/(2k)$ copies of $K_{k,k}$.

This proposes a concrete extremal family for all sufficiently large $k$ in the divisible-order case. The source gives no resolution.

record.title: Unique minimum conjecture for the proportion of problematic stations
record.statement:
Let $K$ be the system capacity, let $\rho_V$ denote the traffic-related parameter, and let $P_b(\rho_V)$ be the proportion of problematic stations as a function of $\rho_V$. The parameter $s$ is the corresponding traffic variable, and $\rho_V=1$ is the symmetry point.

**Unique minimum conjecture.** For every $\frac{\lambda}{\mu}>0$, $P_b$ has a unique minimum $P_b^*$, attained at $\rho_V=1$.

The preceding proposition establishes an extremum at $\rho_V=1$, while uniqueness and the fact that this extremum is a minimum are expected to follow from convexity of the parametric curve. That convexity remains to be proved because $\rho_V$ and $\rho_R$ are related implicitly.

record.title: Existence of the limiting expected weight of k edge-disjoint spanning trees
record.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, with independent edge lengths uniformly distributed on $[0,1]$. Let $\operatorname{mst}_k(K_n)$ denote the expected minimum total length of $k$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, and define

$$
\mu_k^*=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{mst}_k(K_n),\qquad \mu_k^{**}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{mst}_k(K_n).
$$

**Existence conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, one has

$$
\mu_k^*=\mu_k^{**},
$$

i.e. the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{mst}_k(K_n)$ exists.
The case $k=1$ is known, with limit $\zeta(3)$, while the paper studies the more difficult cases $k\geq 2$; the source provides no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: Maximal covering density of the lattices $LD_n$ among covering maxima
record.statement: For each $n\geq 6$, let $LD_n$ be the lattice defined in Dutour (2005), and let a **covering maximum** be a lattice whose covering density decreases under perturbation. **The covering-density conjecture for $LD_n$.** The lattice $LD_n$ has maximal covering density among all covering maxima. This is motivated by the identification of $LD_n$ as a covering maximum and by the theorem classifying the seven-dimensional perfect Delaunay polytopes; partial enumerations in dimensions $8$, $9$, and $10$ support the conjecture, but the claim is not stated as resolved.
record.source_name: Mathieu Dutour Sikiric, “The seven dimensional perfect Delaunay polytopes and Delaunay simplices”, arXiv:1505.03687 (2016).

record.title: Cao–Dehmer–Schaumann's extremal degree-based entropy conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ vertices, and let $l>0$. Here $P_n$ and $S_n$ denote the path and star on $n$ vertices, respectively, and $I_{f^l_d}$ is the degree-based graph entropy.

**Cao–Dehmer–Schaumann's conjecture.** We have

$$
I_{f^l_d}(T)\leq I_{f^l_d}(P_n),
$$

with equality if and only if $T\cong P_n$, and

$$
I_{f^l_d}(T)\geq I_{f^l_d}(S_n),
$$

with equality if and only if $T\cong S_n$.

The conjecture was proposed on the basis of numerical experiments after several unsuccessful attempts at a proof. It asserts that, for every positive exponent, paths and stars give the maximum and minimum degree-based entropies among trees, respectively.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li and Meiqin Wei, “A survey of recent results in (generalized) graph entropies”, arXiv:1505.04658 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Original Burr–Erdős conjecture for pairs of bounded-arboricity graphs
record.statement:
For graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$, let $r(H_1,H_2)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every red-blue edge-coloring of $K_n$ contains a red copy of $H_1$ or a blue copy of $H_2$. The **arboricity** of a graph is the minimum number of forests into which its edge set can be partitioned. **Original Burr–Erdős conjecture.** For every natural number $d$, there exists a constant $c$ such that, for every pair of graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ each having arboricity at most $d$,

$$
r(H_1,H_2)\leq c\bigl(|V(H_1)|+|V(H_2)|\bigr).
$$

This is the original pair-version formulation underlying the degenerate-graph perspective. The source presents it as the original conjecture and does not give a resolution here.
record.source_name: Choongbum Lee, “Ramsey numbers of degenerate graphs”, arXiv:1505.04773 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2015).

record.title: Concavity conjecture for the speed of the maximum of frogs with drift
record.statement:
For $p\in[0,1]$, let the frog model with drift parameter $p$ have maximum speed, namely the limiting speed of its rightmost frog, denoted by $v(p)$. **Concavity conjecture.** The speed of the maximum is a concave function of $p$; that is, for all $p_1,p_2\in[0,1]$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$, 

$$
v(\lambda p_1+(1-\lambda)p_2)\geq \lambda v(p_1)+(1-\lambda)v(p_2).
$$

The paper presents this as an open problem motivated by simulations and a heuristic involving a stationary distribution of the number of frogs at the maximum; it does not establish the claimed concavity.
record.source_name: Thomas Höfelsauer and Felizitas Weidner, “The speed of frogs with drift on Z”, arXiv:1505.05006 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05006

record.title: Pair-distribution conjecture for the two-nut caching game
record.statement: Assume $k=j=2$, so the hider caches two nuts and the searcher aims to find both. A hiding strategy is represented by pairs $(y_1,y_2)$ of depths, with the hole placements randomized as described in the source. **Pair-distribution conjecture.** For every $n$ and $h$, there exists an optimal hiding strategy that is a probability distribution over such pairs, with the two holes selected uniformly from the ${n+1\choose2}$ choices and the two possible depth assignments symmetrized; if the same hole is selected twice, one nut is placed at depth $1$. This is presented as a simplifying structural conjecture; the source says it does not seem difficult but gives no proof.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, “Limit theory of discrete mathematics problems”, arXiv:1505.06984 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.06984

record.title: Pin's generalized synchronizing automaton conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A=(Q,\Sigma)$ be a finite automaton with $n=|Q|$ states. Its rank $r$ is the minimum rank of its input words, where the rank of an input word is the cardinality of the image of its associated mapping. A terminal word is an input word attaining this minimum rank. **Pin's conjecture.** Every $n$-state automaton of rank $r$ has a terminal word of length at most

$$
(n-r)^2.
$$

This generalizes the synchronizing case, since rank-one automata are synchronizing and terminal words are then reset words. The supplied status evidence says that this generalized conjecture was disproved by Kari (2001).
record.source_name: Nasim Karimi, “Reaching the minimum ideal in a finite semigroup”, arXiv:1506.01633 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.01633

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2015). “This generalized conjecture was disproved by Kari .”

record.title: Greedy-partition bound for K4-free graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $K_4$-free graph with $n$ vertices, $e$ edges, and an arbitrary greedy partition $P$ of size $r=r(P)$. Let $t$ and $t_e$ denote the quantities used in the paper's function $g$. **Greedy-partition bound.** It is possible that

$$
t\ge r\bigl(e-r(n-r)\bigr)
$$

and consequently

$$
t_e\ge e-r(n-r).
$$

This is proposed as a possible strengthening of the paper's theorem. The supplied context does not define $t$ or $t_e$ sufficiently to determine the precise combinatorial content or whether the claim has since been resolved.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri and Balázs Keszegh, “On the number of edge-disjoint triangles in K_4-free graphs”, arXiv:1506.03306 (2015).

record.title: Hu, Qi and Shao's monotonicity conjecture for Laplacian eigenvalues of power hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an ordinary graph, let $k=2r$ be even, and let $G^{k}$ be the $k$-th power hypergraph of $G$. For a tensor $\mathcal{T}$, an H-eigenvalue is an eigenvalue having a real eigenvector, and $\lambda(\mathcal{T})$ denotes its largest H-eigenvalue. The Laplacian and signless Laplacian tensors of $G^k$ are denoted by $\mathcal{L}(G^k)$ and $\mathcal{Q}(G^k)$, respectively.

**Hu, Qi and Shao's conjecture.** The sequence

$$
\{\lambda(\mathcal{L}(G^{k}))=\lambda(\mathcal{Q}(G^{k}))\}
$$

is strictly decreasing.

Hu, Qi and Shao established this behavior for cycles and stars and conjectured it for every ordinary graph $G$. The paper under consideration is devoted to proving this conjecture, so the claim is mathematically resolved, although the supplied parser status is unknown.
record.source_name: Xiying Yuan, Liqun Qi and Jiayu Shao, “The proof of a conjecture on largest Laplacian and signless Laplacian H-eigenvalues of uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1506.03330 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03330

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The exhaustive classification of planar 4-critical $P_7$-free graphs
record.statement:
A graph is **planar** if it can be embedded in the plane without crossings. A graph is **4-critical** if its chromatic number is 4 and deleting any edge lowers its chromatic number. A graph is $P_7$-free if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to the path $P_7$. **Exhaustive classification conjecture.** The 52 graphs from Table~ are the only planar 4-critical $P_7$-free graphs.

This conjecture concerns the unresolved general planar $P_7$-free case. The authors determined all planar 4-critical $P_7$-free graphs with at most 30 vertices, and the largest graph found in that range has 13 vertices; whether any further graphs exist remains open.
record.source_name: Jan Goedgebeur and Oliver Schaudt, “Exhaustive generation of k-critical H-free graphs”, arXiv:1506.03647 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.03647

record.title: Goubko's extremal degree-sequence conjecture for terminal distance error
record.statement:
For a tree degree sequence $\mathbf{d}$, write $BFS(\mathbf{d})$ for the associated breadth-first-search tree and define

$$
\mathbf{d}(a,b):=(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{a+b},\underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{a},a+b),\qquad a,b\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

Let $TErr$ denote the relative error between the upper and lower bounds for the minimum terminal distance spectral radius. The **extremal degree-sequence conjecture.** For every tree degree sequence $\mathbf{d}$ there exist $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
TErr(BFS(\mathbf{d}))\leq TErr(BFS(\mathbf{d}(a,b))).
$$

This conjecture is used to justify the paper's $3\%$ error estimate and is explicitly described as an open issue in the analysis.
record.source_name: Mikhail Goubko, “On Minimum Terminal Distance Spectral Radius of Trees with Given Degree Sequence”, arXiv:1507.01733 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.01733

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).

record.title: Symmetric-matrix extension of the quadratic theorem for totally real algebraic integers
record.statement:
Work over $\mathbb{C}$. For a totally real algebraic integer $\lambda$ of degree $d>1$, let $E_s(n,\lambda)$ be the maximum multiplicity of $\lambda$ as an eigenvalue of an $n$-vertex graph. **Symmetric-matrix quadratic conjecture.** The extension of Theorem 3.3 to symmetric matrices holds for totally real algebraic integers; in particular, for $d>1$,

$$
E_s(n,\lambda)\geq n/d-o(n).
$$

The paper proves this assertion for degrees $d\leq4$ and for all representable $\lambda$, where representability means that some integral symmetric matrix has eigenvalues exactly $\lambda$ and its conjugates. The general case is left open in the source.
record.source_name: Boris Bukh, “Ranks of matrices with few distinct entries”, arXiv:1508.00145 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.00145

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2015). “However, Dobrowolski disproved the conjecture.”

record.title: The list neighbour sum distinguishing total colouring problem
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. In the natural list version of neighbour sum distinguishing total colouring, colours are chosen from arbitrary lists of real numbers, and the corresponding list parameter is defined by requiring a proper total colouring whose weighted degrees distinguish adjacent vertices. **List version problem.** The natural list correspondent of $\chi”_{\sum}(G)$ is bounded from above by

$$
(1+o(1))\Delta.
$$

The source presents this as an interesting problem rather than an established result; its methods for the ordinary parameter do not apply to the list version.
record.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “Asymptotically optimal neighbour sum distinguishing total colourings of graphs”, arXiv:1508.01062 (2015).

record.title: Maximal even $(\bar p,\bar q)$-core partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes. A partition is a $(\bar p,\bar q)$-core partition if it is simultaneously a $\bar p$-core and a $\bar q$-core, and it is **even** when its corresponding parity is even. **Maximal even core conjecture.** There exists a $(\bar p,\bar q)$-core partition $\lambda$ such that every even $(\bar p,\bar q)$-core partition is contained in $\lambda$.

This asks whether the even core partitions admit a common largest member under containment, analogous to the known result for all $(\bar p,\bar q)$-core partitions. The source presents this as a future direction and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Calvin Deng, “Even (s, t)-core partitions and self-associate characters of S_n”, arXiv:1508.01462 (2016).

record.title: Even-dimensional k-resultant modulus exponent conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\beta_k(d)$ denote the exponent governing the smallest size of a subset of $\mathbb{F}_q^d$ required to ensure that its $k$-resultant modulus set has the relevant full-size property, where $d\geq2$ is even and $k\geq2$ is an integer. **Even-dimensional $k$-resultant modulus exponent conjecture.** If $d\geq2$ is even, then

$$
\beta_k(d)=\frac d2
$$

for every integer $k\geq2$. This conjecture concerns the sharp threshold in even dimensions for the $k$-resultant modulus set problem; the cited prior work establishes the corresponding two-resultant case, while the assertion for all $k\geq2$ is presented as open here.
record.source_name: David Covert, Doowon Koh and Youngjin Pi, “The k-resultant modulus set problem on algebraic varieties over finite fields”, arXiv:1508.02688 (2015).

record.title: Żak's graph-packing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be graphs on $n$ vertices, and let $E(G_i)$ and $\Delta(G_i)$ denote the edge set and maximum degree of $G_i$, respectively. Two graphs **pack** if there is a bijection between their vertex sets that maps every edge of $G_1$ to a non-edge of $G_2$. **Żak's graph-packing conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta(G_1),\Delta(G_2)\leq n-2
$$

and

$$
|E(G_1)|+|E(G_2)|+\max\{\Delta(G_1),\Delta(G_2)\}\leq 3n-7,
$$

then $G_1$ and $G_2$ pack. Żak's preceding theorem proves the same sufficient condition with $3n-7$ replaced by $3n-96n^{3/4}-65$, so the conjecture asks for the sharp constant bound; the source provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri, Alexandr Kostochka, Andrew McConvey and Derrek Yager, “Toward Żak's conjecture on graph packing”, arXiv:1508.03672 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.03672

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for zero terms in the smallest-representation sequence
record.statement:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime. For each $n\geq1$, let $s(n)$ be the smallest integer $k\geq3$ such that $p_n+k-3$ is represented by $F_k=x_1\cdots x_k+x_1+\cdots+x_k$, and set $s(n)=0$ if no such $k$ exists. The sequence begins

$$
0,0,0,0,0,0,0,3,4,3,0,0,4,0,3,0,3,3,0,4,3,3,4,3,4,0,3,5,3,4,3,\ldots.
$$

**Finiteness conjecture.** The sequence $s(n)$ contains only finitely many zero terms. This asserts that $p_n+k-3$ is represented by $F_k$ for some $k\geq3$ for all but finitely many primes $p_n$.
record.source_name: Vladimir Shevelev, “Representation of positive integers by the form x_1...x_k + x_1 + ... + x_k”, arXiv:1508.03970 (2015).

record.title: The tournament scheduling conjecture for on-line scheduling
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a non-edgeless multigraph, let $t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\chi_{\textit{OL}}^t(G)$ denote the worst-case number of rounds required for on-line scheduling when each vertex is allowed $t$ absences. Let $\chi'(G)$ be the chromatic index of $G$. **On-line scheduling conjecture.** For every such $G$ and $t$, 

$$
\chi_{\textit{OL}}^t(G)=\chi'(G)+2t.
$$

This is described as a weakening of the on-line List Edge Coloring Conjecture and would determine the on-line scheduling number for all non-edgeless multigraphs once the chromatic index is known. The source gives no resolution; it notes that the equality is known in several special cases.
record.source_name: Uwe Schauz, “The Tournament Scheduling Problem with Absences”, arXiv:1509.00488 (2016).

record.title: Conjecture on the extremal function of 2-regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $2$-regular graph, and let $\operatorname{odd}(H)$ be the number of odd components of $H$. The extremal function $c(H)$ is the supremum of $e(G)/v(G)$ over non-null graphs $G$ containing no $H$-minor.

**Extremal-function conjecture.** One has

$$
c(H)=\frac{v(H)+\operatorname{odd}(H)}{2}-1,
$$

unless $H=C_{2l}$, in which case

$$
c(H)=\frac{2l-1}{2},
$$

or $H=kC_4$, in which case

$$
c(H)=2k-\frac12.
$$

If true, this would determine the extremal function for all $2$-regular graphs. The source describes it as a stronger conjecture differing slightly from an earlier conjecture, and gives no resolution in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, Irene Lo, Sergey Norin, Hehui Wu and Liana Yepremyan, “The extremal function for disconnected minors”, arXiv:1509.01185 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01185

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2015).

record.title: Mazzuoccolo's excessive-index conjecture for r-graphs
record.statement:
Let $r$ be a positive integer, let $G$ be an $r$-graph, and let $\chi'_e(G)$ denote the **excessive index** of $G$, namely the minimum number of 1-factors needed to cover $E(G)$. **Mazzuoccolo's excessive-index conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_e(G)\leq 2r-1
$$

for every $r$-graph $G$.

This upper bound is best possible, and the conjecture is equivalent to the generalized Berge–Fulkerson conjecture. The paper states that the existence of a positive integer $k$ bounding $\chi'_e(G)$ for every $r$-graph remains open.
record.source_name: Ligang Jin and Eckhard Steffen, “Unions of 1-factors in r-graphs and overfull graphs”, arXiv:1509.01823 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01823

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2015). “However, it is an open question whether there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $\chi'_e(G)\leq k$ for every $r$-graph $G$.”

record.title: Cubical-distance conjecture for largest minors
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}\subset {[n]\choose k}$ be an arrangement of largest minors, and let $W\in {[n]\choose k}$. Say that $W$ is $(\geq t,\mathcal{J})$-largest if, for every arrangement of minors ending at $\mathcal{J}$, it is absent from the final $t-1$ arrangements. For a maximal arrangement $\mathcal{J}$ of largest minors and $W\notin\mathcal{J}$, let $cube_d(W,\mathcal{J})$ denote their cubical distance. **Cubical-distance conjecture.** If

$$
cube_d(W,\mathcal{J})=t,
$$

then $W$ is $(\geq t+1,\mathcal{J})$-largest minor. This conjecture predicts that cubical distance from a maximal arrangement controls how far below the largest minors an omitted minor lies. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Miriam Farber and Yelena Mandelshtam, “Arrangements Of Minors In The Positive Grassmannian And a Triangulation of The Hypersimplex”, arXiv:1509.02600 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.02600

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2015). “This conjecture was proved independently in and in .”

record.title: The unique-fixed-point conjecture for local belief propagation
record.statement:
Let $\rho$ denote the cluster-size parameter, let $\theta$ and $
u$ be model parameters, let $\theta+
u$ determine the recursion parameter $
u$, and let $\theta+
u h(v)$ be the scalar belief-propagation recursion, where $h$ is the function defined in the paper. A fixed point is a value $v$ satisfying

$$
v=\theta+\lambda h(v).
$$

**Unique-fixed-point conjecture.** If $mu=nu$, then this recursion has a unique fixed point for every

$$
\rho\in(0,1/2)\cup(1/2,1).
$$

A unique fixed point would imply that local belief propagation is optimal in the corresponding unequal-cluster-size cases. The claim is motivated by numerical experiments and is presented in the paper as an open problem; its resolution is not supplied here.
